institution: China Scholarship Council (CSC) / Chinese Government Scholarship; Central Conservatory of Music (CCOM) among …
programme: Chinese Government Scholarship (CSC) — Master's in music / music technology
stillExists2027: YES — annual scheme, runs every cycle. The 2026/2027 round opened Oct 2025 with embassy (Type A) deadlines clustered early-to-mid February 2026; the 2027/2028 round will follow the same pattern.
awards: Not a degree in itself. It is a funding scheme that pays for a Chinese university master's degree. Awarded degree depends on the host institution (e.g. CCOM Master of Arts).
tunisianEligibility: YES on nationality — open to all non-Chinese nationals in good health. Tunisia has a bilateral Type A (embassy) channel via the Chinese Embassy in Tunis.
acceptsSoftwareEngineeringBachelor: CASE-BY-CASE — the scholarship itself only requires 'a bachelor's degree and be under the age of 35' for master's applicants. The subject gate is set by the host conservatory, not by CSC. CCOM and the other music conservatories set their own disciplinary entry bar and normally expect a music background.
liveAudition: DEPENDS ON HOST — CSC itself has no audition. Chinese conservatories (CCOM, Shanghai Conservatory) run their own entrance assessment for music majors; for performance/composition majors this is normally an audition or recorded-performance assessment. UNVERIFIED at the individual-conservatory level for 2027 — the 2027 CCOM international prospectus is not yet published.
portfolioSpec: UNVERIFIED for 2027. CSC application itself requires: passport copy, notarised highest degree certificate, transcripts, study plan (min. 800 words), two recommendation letters from associate professors or above, Foreigner Physical Examination Form, language certificate (HSK for Chinese-taught programmes). Music applicants must additionally supply the host conservatory's own materials.
costForTunisian: ZERO if awarded. Full tuition waiver, on-campus accommodation (single room at master's level at CCOM), comprehensive medical insurance (CNY 800/yr), and a monthly stipend of CNY 3,000 at master's level. If not awarded, self-funded international tuition at Chinese conservatories is typically CNY 40,000–60,000/yr — UNVERIFIED for CCOM 2027.
funding: The scheme IS the funding. Monthly stipend CNY 3,000 (master's), tuition waived, accommodation provided. Age cap: 'Age limits for ... Masters degree is 35 year' — the candidate at 24–26 is comfortably inside.
fundingIsAutomatic: SEPARATE APPLICATION — CSC is applied for in parallel with (or ahead of) university admission. Type A goes through the Chinese Embassy in Tunis with a national quota; Type B goes direct to a designated university. Both require the CSC online portal (www.campuschina.org) plus the university's own application.
deadline: PRIOR CYCLE pattern: embassy (Type A) deadlines fell in early February (roughly 8–15 February 2026 depending on embassy); university (Type B) deadlines run to late March/April; the CCOM-specific portal is cited as opening November with a 30 April cutoff. The Tunis embassy sets the operative Type A date — CONFIRM WITH EMBASSY. 2027 dates not yet published.
languageOfInstruction: Chinese for the large majority of conservatory master's programmes; English-taught music technology master's in China are rare. HSK 4–5 normally required for Chinese-medium study. CSC funds a one-year preparatory Chinese course where the programme demands it, extending total time.
languageCertificate: HSK (level set by host university, typically HSK 4 or 5) for Chinese-taught tracks; IELTS/TOEFL for the few English-taught tracks.
verdictWhy: The scholarship money and the age cap are fine, but the scheme places him nowhere by itself — he still has to be admitted by a Chinese conservatory that will almost certainly want a music background and a Chinese-language qualification he does not have. Add a probable preparatory Chinese year on top and the September 2027 start slips to 2028. There is no identified English-taught electronic-music master's in China that would take a software-engineering BSc.
correction: The input row records cost as 'Not published' and gate as 'None found in the text'. Both are misleading: the CSC funding package is fully published (CNY 3,000/month plus tuition and housing at master's level), and the real gate is not the scholarship at all but the host conservatory's own entrance assessment, which for music majors is normally an audition. Treating this as a low-gate option is wrong.

institution: NIIED — National Institute for International Education (Korean government)

What is unresolved is that no English-taught Korean electronic-music or music-technology master's has been identified that would admit a software-engineering BSc, and the compulsory Korean language year pushes actual degree start to 2028. Name a specific host programme before spending effort on this.
correction: The input row lists 'cost: Not published' and 'gate: None found in the text'. The package is fully published (airfare, full tuition, monthly allowance, Korean language year, insurance, settlement allowance) and the real gate is the university placement plus the compulsory Korean language year, not the scholarship. Also correct: Tunisia DOES have an embassy-track GKS-G quota (6 places, 2026 table) — some secondary sources wrongly state Tunisia has no quota, which is true only for the undergraduate GKS-U strand.

programme: Sound Design for Audiovisual Media / Tonmeister*in für audiovisuelle Medien
stillExists2027: YES — and the 2027 application window is already published: 'Applications are accepted only once a year for the winter semester. The application period begins on 12 April and ends on 18 May 2027.' Entry is winter term only.
awards: A real second-cycle degree: 'Degree: Master of Fine Arts (M.F.A.)'. Note the unusual length — 'Program Duration: 6 Semester (120 LP)', i.e. three years for 120 ECTS.
acceptsSoftwareEngineeringBachelor: NO. The requirement is 'Proof (PDF) of a completed Bachelor of Fine Arts (B.F.A.) degree in Sound, Tonmeister*in or a comparable subject-specific degree'. A BSc Software Engineering is not a comparable subject-specific degree in sound. Compounded by a hard practical prerequisite: 'The ability to play keyboard instruments is prerequisite.'
liveAudition: YES, in substance — an on-site three-part Eignungsprüfung. Part 1 is a music test covering interval identification and piano performance; Part 2 is an interview presenting the submitted works (this part may be held by video conference); Part 3 is a practical examination requiring the applicant to compose a score for film in Pro Tools. Parts 1 and 3 are on site. Part 1 is a live playing-and-ear test — precisely the gate the candidate cannot pass.
portfolioSpec: Documentation of 12 pages maximum; video samples totalling 15 minutes showing at least three films on which the applicant was responsible for sound design; plus one music piece self-recorded and self-mixed. Deadline 18 May 2027.
costForTunisian: No tuition — German state Filmuniversität. Semester contribution (Semesterbeitrag) only, not stated on the programme page — UNVERIFIED, but German public institutions typically charge EUR 250–350/semester including the Berlin/Brandenburg transport ticket.
funding: None stated by the programme. DAAD Study Scholarships for Artists would be the external route (separate, earlier application, roughly EUR 992/month) — but they presuppose an artistic degree the candidate lacks.
deadline: 12 April 2027 – 18 May 2027, for winter semester 2027/28 entry.
languageOfInstruction: German. Required certificate: DSH-1 or equivalent; a B1 certificate is accepted at application time if the higher certificate is not yet available.
verdictWhy: This one fails on three independent gates at once: it demands a BFA in Sound or Tonmeister, it demands German at DSH-1, and its entrance exam includes live piano playing and interval identification plus an on-site Pro Tools scoring test. The portfolio brief alone — three films where he led the sound design — presumes a career he has not started. There is no path in for him by September 2027.
correction: The input row records the gate as 'Exam/interview only'. That understates it badly: the Eignungsprüfung is a three-part on-site examination whose first component is a live music test with piano performance, which is functionally an audition. It also omits the hard subject bar (BFA in Sound/Tonmeister) and the DSH-1 German requirement — either of which alone disqualifies this candidate.

institution: Hochschule für Musik und Theater »Felix Mendelssohn Bartholdy« Leipzig (HMT Leipzig)
stillExists2027: YES — 'Elektroakustische Musik (konsekutiv künstlerisch): 4 Semester', listed in the current Komposition/Musiktheorie/Improvisation admission-conditions document.
awards: A real second-cycle degree: 'Abschluss: Master of Music', four semesters, consecutive artistic master's.
acceptsSoftwareEngineeringBachelor: NO. The document states the master's builds on 'einem abgeschlossenen Bachelor- oder gleichwertigem Studium in einem künstlerisch relevanten Fach' — a completed bachelor or equivalent in an ARTISTICALLY RELEVANT subject. A BSc Software Engineering is not artistically relevant on any ordinary reading, and HMT reserves the right to test musical background broadly: 'Sie hat das Recht, die musikalischen Vorkenntnisse umfassend zu überprüfen.'
liveAudition: NO AUDITION in the performance sense — and this is the genuinely useful distinction here. Unlike the Komposition and Tonsatz tracks at the same institute, the Elektroakustische Musik master's has NO instrument test and NO Gehörbildung (ear-training) component. Its Hauptprüfung is a single oral examination of about 40 minutes: presentation and short analysis of one of the applicant's own pieces with attention to the electroacoustic means used (approx. 10 minutes); a discussion of theoretical questions and the history of electroacoustic music; demonstration of basic knowledge in acoustics and studio technique; and aural analysis of electroacoustic examples from recordings. That is an oral exam, not an audition. But it is on site and it is in German.
portfolioSpec: 'mindestens drei eigene Kompositionen mit wesentlichen elektroakustischen Anteilen möglichst unterschiedlicher Gattungen (z.B. Fixed Media, Live-Elektronik, Computermusik/algorithmische Komposition)' — at least three own compositions with substantial electroacoustic content, in as many different genres as possible, e.g. fixed media, live electronics, computer music/algorithmic composition. Plus an analytical commentary on one of the pieces IN GERMAN, and at least one piece supplied as a .wav audio file. Submitted digitally via the online portal with the admission application. No per-piece duration is specified.
costForTunisian: No tuition — Saxon state institution. Semester contribution only; exact amount not stated in the admission document — UNVERIFIED.
funding: None stated. DAAD would be the external route, separate and earlier.
deadline: Not stated in the admission-conditions document — UNVERIFIED. German Musikhochschule master's deadlines for a winter-semester start typically fall between mid-February and 1 April; confirm with Christa Franz (Christa.Franz@hmt-leipzig.de, +49 341 2144 622).
languageOfInstruction: German. 'Sprachkenntnisse (für ausländische Bewerber): Nachweis Stufe B1 des Gemeinsamen Europäischen Referenzrahmens für Sprachen (GER)' — B1 German for foreign applicants, which is a relatively low bar by German conservatory standards. But the written analytical commentary must be produced in German and the 40-minute oral exam is in German.
verdictWhy: The exam design is unusually favourable — no instrument, no ear training, just a 40-minute oral on your own electroacoustic work — and the German bar is only B1, so on paper this is the most passable German conservatory route in this batch. It still fails on the entry rule: the master's is explicitly built on a bachelor in an artistically relevant subject, and software engineering is not that. He also has no three finished electroacoustic works and no German at all today.
correction: The input row records the gate as 'Portfolio + exam/interview'. That is right in shape but the record should say plainly that the Elektroakustische Musik track carries NO audition, NO instrument test and NO ear-training test, unlike every other Komposition track at the same institute — this is a materially different gate from the sibling programmes and the sweep flattened it. The blocking factor is the 'künstlerisch relevantes Fach' bachelor rule plus B1 German, not a performance test.

institution: Kunstuniversität Graz (KUG) — Institut für Elektronische Musik und Akustik (IEM)
programme: Computermusik und Klangkunst (Computer Music and Sound Art)
stillExists2027: YES — current MA, study code UV 066 705, 4 semesters, 120 ECTS, entry to winter semester.
awards: A real second-cycle degree: Master of Arts, 120 ECTS over 4 semesters, with its own published curriculum (Curriculum_Computermusik_Klangkunst_MA).
acceptsSoftwareEngineeringBachelor: CASE-BY-CASE — and this is the most open door in the batch. KUG does not require a music bachelor by name; it assesses 'Gleichwertigkeit des Vorstudiums' (equivalence of prior study) on a case-by-case basis, and the admission decision rests principally on the artistic entrance examination rather than on the subject of the first degree. IEM is an electronic-music and acoustics institute with a strong engineering culture, which makes a software-engineering background legible rather than disqualifying. It is not a guarantee — equivalence can be refused or made conditional on supplementary examinations.
liveAudition: NO. This is the decisive finding and it separates KUG from every conservatory in this batch. The Zulassungsprüfung is held ONLINE via Zoom and consists of 'ein Gespräch' — a conversation, conducted in German OR ENGLISH, based on the two submitted works, in which the applicant explains their motivation and intended focus. There is no instrument test, no ear-training test, no performance, and no travel to Graz.
portfolioSpec: 'zwei aussagekräftige Beispiele deiner künstlerischen Arbeit' — TWO compelling examples of artistic work: compositions, improvisations or sketches in computer music or sound art, EACH APPROXIMATELY 5 MINUTES. Format: audio or video files compressed as mp3, h264 or similar, uploaded as a SINGLE ZIP FILE not exceeding approximately 150 MB. Note that sketches are explicitly acceptable — this is a build brief of roughly ten minutes of finished material, the smallest portfolio requirement found anywhere in this batch.
costForTunisian: EUR 726.72 per semester tuition as a third-country national, plus the ÖH student union fee of EUR 26.20 — EUR 752.92 per semester, i.e. EUR 1,505.84 per academic year. (The EUR 363.36 rate and the fee exemption apply only to Austrians, EU/EEA and Swiss nationals, convention refugees, and third-country nationals treated as equivalent.) KUG operates a tuition waiver under its East/South-East Europe focus, which does not cover Tunisia.
funding: Nothing published at programme level that this candidate could win on admission. External routes only (OeAD/Austrian government scholarships, Erasmus+), all separate and earlier applications. Assume he pays the EUR 1,505.84/year himself.
deadline: '1. März bis 1. Mai' — 1 March to 1 May, with the entrance examination held in June, for winter-semester entry. For a September/October 2027 start that means 1 March – 1 May 2027.
languageOfInstruction: German is the university's language of instruction; the entrance examination itself may be held in German or English. Whether the MA can be completed in English is UNVERIFIED, and Austrian universities normally require a German certificate for admission to German-language programmes — the exact level required by KUG could not be reached (the Deutschkenntnisse page returned 404). THIS IS THE OPEN QUESTION and it must be settled before committing.
languageCertificate: UNVERIFIED — KUG's German-language-requirements page could not be reached. Confirm directly with KUG admissions.
